title: Rick & Morty vs React & Angular: Epic Framework Showdown!
caption: React vs Angular? Let Rick & Morty break it down for you! #WebDev

scenes.script: Alright, Morty, let's dive into this React vs Angular mess. It's like comparing a Swiss Army knife to a single, really sharp knife.
Uh, Rick? What do you mean?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty looking to another side without caring.png

scenes.script: Well, React is like that single sharp knife—it's just for the view layer. Facebook made it, and it's great for dynamic UIs with this thing called a virtual DOM.
Oh, so it's like when I built that website where the buttons change color? That was React!
scenes.web_image: javascript library for dynamic user interfaces

scenes.script: Exactly! And it's super scalable. But if you want a full meal, Angular is the Swiss Army knife. Google made it, and it's got two-way data binding, dependency injection—the works!
Wait, so Angular is like when I used that tool where everything connects automatically?
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty with a dumb looking without understanding.png

scenes.script: Yes! And it uses TypeScript, which is like JavaScript on steroids. React? Just JSX—JavaScript and HTML-like syntax.
So if I need a simple website, use React. If it's for the big leagues, Angular?
Bingo! And remember, Morty: React needs extra libraries for state management and routing. Angular’s got it all built-in.
scenes.web_image: comparison of React and Angular features

scenes.script: Got it! So, like choosing between a car or a bike?
Exactly! A bike for speed and simplicity—React. A car for the whole package—Angular.
Alright, Rick. I think I got it this time.
scenes.character_image: volume/resources/LoreLabs/images/morty/morty with a dumb looking without understanding.png

topic: What is the difference between React and Angular?
